name: Yugh
world_status: statement found in an open source
sweep_summary: Yugh (yugh1239) is not in the catalog. The single listed item, Werner 1996 'Vergleichende Akzentologie der Jenissej-Sprachen', is squarely about Yeniseian (Yugh + Ket) accent: Google Books snippet view gives its TOC ('Die Tonalität des Jugischen und Ketischen' p. 12; 'Die Wechselwirkung des Tonal- und Phonemsystems' p. 34) and one Yugh-relevant snippet (p. 65: Russian loans with final stress, jug. kurgóm, kùrpá, lapsá, 'mostly receive the accentuation type [..]'), but the native-accent chapters are unreachable (snippet-only, Google then blocked; HathiTrust search-only behind an automated-access block; no review; no archive.org copy) — priority high, together with Werner 1997 'Das Jugische' (HathiTrust search-only). The best first-hand statement actually read is Werner's own 1997 Russian sketch (Языки мира, p. 189 §2.1.2, scan held by the project, verified against the page scan): four syllable tones; in polysyllables the tone survives only in the stressed syllable so 'stress is essentially a measure of the completeness of tone realisation'; two short-syllable accent types, pitch rise on the first (stressed) syllable (sounds like dynamic word stress) vs on the last/penultimate syllable (dʌnyŋ 'knives', kanča 'pipe'); function morphemes mostly unstressed (p. 190). Not obtained: Werner 1980 (verb-paradigm accentuation in Yugh, Tomsk; TSU repository bot-gated), Werner 1979 and 1977 (Tomsk/Leningrad), Werner & Vajda 2012 dictionary (lending-restricted), Vajda 2024 De Gruyter chapter (paywalled). All downloads and probes are.

new_statements.quote: Наиболее четко тоны реализуются в изолированных односложных словах; в многосложных словах они могут сохраняться лишь в ударных слогах. В последнем случае ударение является по существу мерой полноты реализации тона. Иное положение наблюдается при реализации двух особых краткосложных акцентных типов: при одном из них наблюдается повышение основного тона голоса на первом (ударном) слоге, при другом — на последнем или предпоследнем (ударном) слоге при одинаковой интенсивности во всех слогах: dʌnyŋ ‘ножи’, kanča ‘курительная трубка’. Первый тип производит впечатление динамического словесного ударения.
new_statements.translation: Tones are realized most clearly in isolated monosyllabic words; in polysyllabic words they can be preserved only in stressed syllables. In the latter case stress is essentially a measure of the completeness of tone realization. A different situation is observed in the realization of two special short-syllable accent types: in one of them a rise of the fundamental frequency of the voice is observed on the first (stressed) syllable, in the other on the last or penultimate (stressed) syllable with equal intensity in all syllables: dʌnyŋ 'knives', kanča 'smoking pipe'. The first type gives the impression of dynamic word stress.
new_statements.citation: Вернер Г. К. 1997. Югский язык. In: А. П. Володин, Н. Б. Вахтин, А. А. Кибрик (eds.), Языки мира: Палеоазиатские языки. Москва: Индрик, pp. 187-195.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Yugh has four syllable tones (high register / pharyngealization / circumflex contour / abruptness). Word stress is not given a positional rule: in polysyllabic words the stressed syllable is the one on which the tone is (fully) realized, i.e. stress is a by-product of tone realization on the tonic (root) syllable; function morphemes are mostly unstressed (§2.2.2, p. 190), and the RAS minlang portal adds that tones occur only on the first syllable of the root morpheme. Alongside this, two 'short-syllable accent types' exist in which an F0 peak falls either on the first syllable or on the final/penultimate syllable with even intensity; only the first of these sounds like dynamic word stress.
new_statements.exceptions: Two short-syllable accent types (F0 rise on first syllable vs. on last or penultimate syllable) contrast with the tone-borne stress; function (auxiliary) morphemes usually unstressed (p. 190). No positional exceptions listed.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level; tones fully realized only in isolated monosyllables (citation forms), reduced to the stressed syllable in polysyllabic words. Unstressed syllables have a reduced vowel inventory (7 of 10 vowels, §2.1.3).
new_statements.identity_note: Werner's chapter describes Yugh as the language of the 'Sym Kets' (сымские кеты; self-name juɣun), formerly treated as the Sym dialect of Ket, recorded from the last families in Yartsevo and Vorogovo (Krasnoyarsk Krai) up to the mid-1970s; this is exactly yugh1239 (ISO yug). Note: a parallel our files (retired Glottolog code) already holds the same Rosetta scans and reached the same passage; the yugh1239 files were downloaded and scanned afresh here.

new_statements.quote: В многосложных словах они [тоны] могут сохраняться лишь в ударных слогах. В последнем случае ударение является по существу мерой полноты реализации тона. Иное положение наблюдается при реализации двух особых краткосложных акцентных типов: при одном из них наблюдается повышение основного тона голоса на первом (ударном) слоге, при другом — на последнем или предпоследнем (ударном) слоге при одинаковой интенсивности во всех слогах: dʌnyŋ ‘ножи’, kanča ‘курительная трубка’. Первый тип производит впечатление динамического словесного ударения.
new_statements.translation: In polysyllabic words they [the tones] can be preserved only in stressed syllables. In the latter case stress is essentially a measure of the completeness of the tone's realisation. A different situation is observed in the realisation of two special short-syllable accent types: in one of them a rise of the fundamental pitch of the voice is observed on the first (stressed) syllable, in the other on the last or penultimate (stressed) syllable, with equal intensity in all syllables: dʌnyŋ 'knives', kanča 'tobacco pipe'. The first type gives the impression of dynamic word stress.
new_statements.citation: Вернер, Г. К. 1997. Югский язык. In Языки мира: Палеоазиатские языки, 187–195. Москва: Индрик.
new_statements.reading: Yugh is a syllable-tone language (four tones); word-level prominence is the syllable that carries the full tone, and Werner explicitly reduces 'stress' to the degree of tone realisation rather than an independent positional rule. Beyond that, two short-syllable accent types exist: pitch rise on the first (stressed) syllable — the one that sounds like dynamic word stress — versus pitch rise on the final or penultimate syllable (dʌnyŋ, kanča). Function morphemes (semi-suffix -dʼeŋ etc.) are mostly unstressed (p. 190 §2.2.2). For a stress typology this reads as tone/pitch accent with lexically distributed placement (predominantly root-initial, minority final/penult), not a fixed-position system.

tone_statements.citation: Вернер Г. К. 1997. Енисейские языки. In: А. П. Володин, Н. Б. Вахтин, А. А. Кибрик (eds.), Языки мира: Палеоазиатские языки. Москва: Индрик, pp. 169–177. [online text: philology.ru]
tone_statements.quote: Для енисейского вокализма характерны четыре ступени подъема языка и наличие чередований аблаутного характера. Обе эти особенности исторически связаны со слоговой акцентуацией (слоговыми тонами), которая резко отличает Е.я. от окружающих, в которых в свою очередь представлена гармония гласных, отсутствующая в Е.я. В Е.я. широко используются слоговые тоновые оппозиции для дифференциации лексических единиц и форм числа имени, например: юж.-кет. 1 s'ul' 'кровь', 2 s'u ? l' 'нельма', 3 s'u:l' 'нарта', 4 s'ul' 'крюк для детской люльки'; югск. 1 tap 'обруч', мн. ч. 4 ta:p .
tone_statements.translation: Yeniseian vocalism is characterised by four degrees of tongue height and by alternations of an ablaut character. Both features are historically connected with syllable accentuation (syllabic tones), which sharply distinguishes the Yeniseian languages from the surrounding ones, which in turn have vowel harmony, absent in Yeniseian. In the Yeniseian languages syllabic tone oppositions are widely used to differentiate lexical units and number forms of the noun, e.g. Southern Ket ¹s'ul' 'blood', ²s'uˀl' 'nelma (fish)', ³s'u:l' 'sledge', ⁴s'ul' 'cradle hook'; Yugh ¹tap 'hoop', pl. ⁴ta:p.

tone_statements.citation: Werner, Heinrich K. 1974. Die Akzentuation der mehrsilbigen Wörter in den gegenwärtigen Jenissei-Dialekten. Zeitschrift für Phonetik, Sprachwissenschaft und Kommunikationsforschung 27(1-3): 379-386. Berlin: Akademie-Verlag. DOI 10.1524/stuf.1974.27.13.379.
tone_statements.quote: ...мы не знаем, были ли эти «тоны» противопоставлены мелодически (как это имеет место в современных языках)... Кетский и югский имеют здесь первый тон (в югском высокий ровный, а в кетском ровный)... Здесь в кетском и югском представлен второй тон (высокий восходящий или восходяще-нисходящий с факультативной гортанной смычкой) с обязательной краткостью гласного... Здесь в кетском и югском налицо четвертый тон. В югском он низкий восходяще-нисходящий, гласный при этом долгий и сильно ларингализованный... В югском и кетском третий тон высокий восходяще-нисходящий, без ларингализации, с долготой гласного.
tone_statements.translation: ...we do not know whether these 'tones' were opposed melodically (as is the case in the modern languages)... Ket and Yugh have here the first tone (in Yugh high level, in Ket level)... Here Ket and Yugh show the second tone (high rising or rising-falling with an optional glottal stop) with obligatory shortness of the vowel... Here Ket and Yugh show the fourth tone. In Yugh it is low rising-falling, the vowel being long and strongly laryngealized... In Yugh and Ket the third tone is high rising-falling, without laryngealization, with vowel length.
tone_statements.locator: section 'Просодия', pp. 202-203 and fn. 42 on p. 205; pagination of the 2007 reprint
tone_statements.summary: Comparative study: gives Yugh values of tones 1-4 on monosyllabic roots and two disyllabic accent types (V, VI: pitch rise on 1st or 2nd syllable); no total count; detail credited to Werner 1974.

В югском и кетском третий тон высокий восходяще-нисходящий, без ларингализации, с долготой гласного.

tone.translation: ...we do not know whether these 'tones' were opposed melodically (as is the case in the modern languages)... Ket and Yugh have here the first tone (in Yugh high level, in Ket level)... Here Ket and Yugh show the second tone (high rising or rising-falling with an optional glottal stop) with obligatory shortness of the vowel... Here Ket and Yugh show the fourth tone. In Yugh it is low rising-falling, the vowel being long and strongly laryngealized... In Yugh and Ket the third tone is high rising-falling, without laryngealization, with vowel length.
